content: The primary cause of otitis externa is bacterial infection, with the majority of cases attributed to Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Staphylococcus aureus. Fungal infections, specifically otomycosis, can also lead to otitis externa. The most common fungal pathogens involved are Candida albicans and Aspergillus niger. Non-infectious otitis externa can result from allergic dermatitis when inflammatory dermatoses, such as eczema, seborrhea, or psoriasis, extend to the ear canal. Contact dermatitis can also cause otitis externa due to allergic reactions to substances such as cosmetic chemicals, metals (especially nickel or silver), or irritants like shampoos, soaps, and other cosmetic products. In rare cases, the psoriasis treatment drug secukinumab has been reported to cause otitis externa as an adverse reaction. Bacterial causes of otitis externa include a wide range of pathogens that can inflame the external ear canal. The primary bacterial culprits are Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. Additional bacterial species that may contribute include Staphylococcus epidermidis, Microbacterium otitidis, Microbacterium alconae, Staphylococcus caprae, Staphylococcus auricularis, Enterococcus faecalis, Enterobacter cloacae, Staphylococcus capitis, and Staphylococcus haemolyticus. Bacteria that thrive in water environments can also facilitate infections by entering the ear canal. Fungal causes of otitis externa, particularly otomycosis, are often seen following prolonged antibiotic therapy. The primary fungal pathogens involved are Candida albicans and Aspergillus niger. Allergic reactions can lead to non-infectious otitis externa when dermatitis spreads to the ear canal. Common conditions include eczema, seborrhea, and psoriasis. Contact dermatitis may occur due to exposure to metals (such as nickel or silver), hearing aids, or chemical irritants like shampoos, soaps, and cosmetics. Lastly, drug interactions, though rare, can also contribute to otitis externa. For example, the psoriasis treatment drug secukinumab has been identified as a potential cause of otitis externa as an adverse effect.
